summary: Persistent 3D subtracts information: Z duplicates stratum while perspective reverses salience, occlusion breaks reference access, and unequal apparent scale corrupts density comparison. Keep the table coplanar and face-on; if three.js is mandatory, use it only for in-plane transitions.

tension_rulings.why: Z is wasteful redundancy because row position and the printed S-token already encode stratum without altering visibility, scale, or comparability.
Set the reference view to a fixed face-on orthographic camera with equal tile scale and zero overlap; any angle or dolly distance that changes those conditions is outside the allowed range.
Flying tiles forward and reassembling them adds theatre to the existing 1..n sequence while temporarily removing the depth and family context that makes the sequence informative.

findings.section: Part 2 — Core idea: depth becomes literal
findings.problem: Mapping stratum to Z adds no independent information, and its redundancy is wasteful because perceiving it requires perspective or parallax that damages the primary table encoding.
findings.instruction: Remove persistent Z-as-stratum and retain row position plus the printed S-token as the complete depth encoding.

findings.section: Part 2 — Core idea and proposed depth parallax
findings.problem: Perspective makes S4 smaller and more occluded precisely because it is deepest, systematically reducing the visibility of the most prerequisite- and trust-laden elements; this is actively misleading.
findings.instruction: Prohibit perspective depth, camera orbit, and parallax in the reference state; render every stratum at identical scale and visibility.

findings.problem: Placing S0's 3 elements and S3's 22 elements at different perspective distances corrupts their apparent-size comparison and conceals the packed layout's central finding.
findings.instruction: Keep all five rows coplanar at one scale so occupied width and tile count remain directly comparable.

findings.problem: Occlusion makes some elements unreachable or incomparable in a reference table; avoiding it while preserving readable faces effectively requires a face-on camera.
findings.instruction: Require a fixed face-on orthographic view with no tile overlap or clipping; if a transition temporarily overlaps tiles, restore the complete coplanar table before interaction resumes.

findings.section: Part 1 — Protocol projection, laws, and hazards
findings.problem: No listed quantity benefits from a third spatial dimension: law and hazard membership are categorical or countable, while protocol build order is a one-dimensional sequence already encoded by numbers.
findings.instruction: Show membership through filtering or badges, counts through aligned bars or numerals, and build order through numbers, an in-plane path, or sequential highlighting; assign none of them to Z.

findings.problem: The assembly and arrangement motions use depth without adding a durable, comparable data relationship, so 3D functions as decoration rather than encoding.
findings.instruction: Do not use 3D for this table; if three.js remains mandatory, constrain it to coplanar in-plane transitions that never change scale, ordering evidence, visibility, or reachability.

what_to_keep: The packed 2D structure in which row means stratum, block means family, and equal-scale occupancy exposes the S0-to-S3 asymmetry.
dissent_note: A motion or branding lens may value spatial spectacle, but spectacle cannot justify corrupting the table's quantitative comparison and reference function.
